headline: COP31 Day-10 draft keeps CCUS and carbon-removal goals but drops fossil-fuel references
summary: The Turkiye/Australia Presidency's revised second draft cover decision retains the bracketed goal to scale CCS to at least ~500 Mt CO2/yr by 2035 and keeps broad carbon-dioxide-removal language, while stripping out explicit fossil-fuel wording, leaving carbon-management provisions among the most contested items heading into the closing plenary.
co2crc_note: A first-ever COP-level CCUS/CDR capacity goal would set the global policy frame CO2CRC's Australian CCS work operates within; Australia co-presides the talks.
extractor_note: 500 Mt is a draft policy target in brackets, not a commitment; capacity_mtpa is a policy-target figure, non-additive. Day-10 development, distinct from the first draft briefed 17-18 Nov.

headline: Reuters asks whether Europe can scale its flagship carbon-capture projects into a viable industrial solution
summary: A Reuters feature weighs whether Europe's marquee CCS schemes can move from demonstration to commercially viable industrial decarbonisation, citing cost, demand and capture plants' dependence on still-incomplete transport-and-storage clusters.
co2crc_note: European commercial-viability debate informs the demand-side and T&S-cluster risks CO2CRC tracks for Australian CCS economics.
extractor_note: Analytical feature, not a discrete event; no money figure.

headline: COP31 carbon-capture target raises fears of prolonged fossil-fuel dependence
summary: African coverage of the Antalya talks reports warnings that the draft cover decision's ~500 Mt CO2/yr CCS goal could entrench fossil-fuel use, with CIEL's Rachel Kennerley arguing the focus on capture technology distracts from phasing out fossil fuels.
co2crc_note: Social-licence pushback on CCS in the COP text is reputationally relevant to CO2CRC's public-engagement work.

headline: New water-tolerant carbon-capture material turns humidity from obstacle to ally
summary: Oregon State University researchers report a metal-organic framework (BVR-X, Angewandte Chemie) that routes water and CO2 into separate pore regions so moisture no longer blocks capture sites, sustaining performance across dozens of cycles in humid exhaust; a patent has been filed.
co2crc_note: Water-tolerant sorbent chemistry is relevant to capture-cost R&D CO2CRC follows, but early-stage.
extractor_note: Radar: underlying news dated 17 Nov, just outside the 19-20 Nov window.
